description: North America's largest and longest-running auto show, held every February at McCormick Place since 1901 and occupying over a million square feet. The 2027 edition is set for February 13-21. What separates it from other shows is that you can actually get in the cars - hundreds of vehicles are open to sit in, and indoor test tracks let you ride along in EVs and trucks without a salesperson attached. It fills nine days including two weekends, and weekday mornings are dramatically calmer. Tickets are sold at the door and online, with reduced pricing for kids and seniors.
highlights: Every February at McCormick Place since 1901
Sit in hundreds of vehicles, no sales pressure
Indoor EV and truck test tracks
why_residents_love_it: A warm, enormous, genuinely fun way to burn a February Saturday - and the best car research you'll ever do.

name: Chicago Restaurant Week
address: Participating restaurants citywide and in the suburbs
distance_note: Dozens of participating restaurants are within a 5-10 minute walk of 401 W Ontario, concentrated along Hubbard, Clark, Wells and Ontario.
description: A 17-day citywide promotion run by Choose Chicago each winter, typically launching in late January and running into early February, when hundreds of restaurants offer prix fixe menus at fixed price points - most recently $30, $45 and $60 for dinner, with lower-priced brunch and lunch menus. It is the single best window to try the tasting-menu and steakhouse rooms that are otherwise a splurge, and River North has one of the densest concentrations of participants in the city. Reservations open a few weeks ahead and the marquee rooms fill within hours, so set a calendar reminder in early January.
highlights: Dozens of participating restaurants in River North alone
why_residents_love_it: The neighborhood's expensive dining rooms become reachable for two and a half weeks, all within walking distance.

name: Taste of Chicago
address: Grant Park, 331 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60601
distance_note: Grant Park is about 1.3 miles southeast - a 25-minute walk, or take the Brown Line to Randolph/Wabash and walk three blocks east.
price_range: Free entry; food tickets typically $10-$30 per person
description: The city's flagship food festival returned to Grant Park for its 46th year, running July 8-12 in 2026 with Common headlining a free concert. Admission is free; you buy tickets in strips and spend them across dozens of restaurant tents, food trucks and pop-ups representing neighborhoods across the city. The smart approach is to skip the giant portions and order the small 'taste' size at five or six booths - that's the whole point. Live music runs all day on multiple stages including the Petrillo Music Shell, and the city has recently added neighborhood pop-up editions in Austin, Pilsen and elsewhere earlier in the summer.
highlights: Free admission, five days in July
Free headliner concerts at Petrillo Music Shell
why_residents_love_it: A five-day excuse to eat your way across all 77 neighborhoods without leaving downtown.

name: Millennium Park Summer Music Series
address: Jay Pritzker Pavilion, Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
distance_note: Millennium Park is about 1.2 miles southeast - a 25-minute walk down Michigan Avenue, or the Brown/Purple Line from Chicago/Franklin to Randolph/Wabash and a three-block walk.
description: All summer long the Frank Gehry-designed Jay Pritzker Pavilion hosts free evening concerts spanning global, indie, soul, gospel and Latin music, with American Sign Language interpretation at every show. Seats in the pavilion bowl and space on the Great Lawn are free and first-come - bring a blanket, a picnic and a bottle of wine, which is permitted. Running alongside it, the Grant Park Music Festival presents ten weeks of free orchestral and choral concerts, June 10 through August 15 in 2026, one of the only free outdoor classical series in the country. Concerts happen rain or shine.
highlights: Free concerts all summer at Pritzker Pavilion
Picnics and wine allowed on the Great Lawn
Grant Park Music Festival's free classical season runs alongside
why_residents_love_it: Free live music several nights a week in the best outdoor room in the city - the default cheap summer date night.

name: Chicago Air and Water Show
address: North Avenue Beach, 1600 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60614
distance_note: North Avenue Beach is about 1.8 miles northeast - a 35-minute walk or 10-minute ride. Ohio Street Beach, only 1.3 miles east, catches most of the show with a fraction of the crowd.
description: The largest free admission air and water show in the United States, running a mid-August weekend every year - the 2026 show was August 15-16. The U.S. Navy Blue Angels and the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds headline in most years, joined by parachute teams, aerobatic acts and jet demonstrations that fly low over the lake. North Avenue Beach is the official viewing center and gets packed by mid-morning, but the show is visible for miles along the lakefront - Oak Street Beach, Ohio Street Beach and Olive Park are all easier bets. Practice runs on the Friday before are nearly as good and far less crowded.
highlights: Friday practice day is the local's secret
why_residents_love_it: Jets scream over the neighborhood all weekend - plenty of River North residents just watch from a rooftop or balcony.

name: Chicago Blues Festival
address: Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
distance_note: Millennium Park is about 1.2 miles southeast - a 25-minute walk down Michigan Avenue, or the Brown/Purple Line from Chicago/Franklin to Randolph/Wabash.
description: The largest free blues festival in the world, and a legitimate point of civic pride in the city that electrified the genre. The 2026 edition ran June 4-7 in Millennium Park, with the Jay Pritzker Pavilion hosting the evening headliners and smaller stages running all afternoon. It is entirely free - claim a spot on the Great Lawn with a blanket, or get into the seating bowl early for the marquee sets. The lineup mixes national legends with the South and West Side players who actually built the sound, and the festival usually spreads satellite programming to neighborhood venues during the same week.
highlights: Largest free blues festival in the world
why_residents_love_it: World-class blues for exactly nothing, a walk away - the city's best free weekend of the year.

name: Chicago Jazz Festival
address: Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
distance_note: Millennium Park is about 1.2 miles southeast - roughly a 25-minute walk, or two stops on the Brown/Purple Line to Randolph/Wabash.
description: Running over Labor Day weekend since 1979, the Chicago Jazz Festival closes out the city's summer with four free days in Millennium Park - September 3-6 in 2026, with a lineup that included Dee Dee Bridgewater, Robert Glasper, the Miles Electric Band and Paquito D'Rivera. Programming spans straight-ahead standards, avant-garde work from the AACM lineage that started here, and international acts. Daytime sets on the smaller stages are where you find the local players worth knowing; the Pritzker Pavilion handles the headliners after dark. Free, first-come seating, no ticket required.
highlights: Deep Chicago avant-garde and AACM roots
Daytime side stages plus Pritzker headliners
why_residents_love_it: The perfect last-weekend-of-summer ritual: a blanket, the Great Lawn, and four days of free jazz.
photo_source: Choose Chicago / City of Chicago (photo: Patrick L. Pyszka)

name: Christkindlmarket Chicago
address: Daley Plaza, 50 W Washington St, Chicago, IL 60602
distance_note: About 1 mile south of 401 W Ontario - a 20-minute walk, or two stops on the Brown/Purple Line from Chicago/Franklin to Washington/Wells and you're across the street.
description: Chicago's German-style Christmas market has filled Daley Plaza every year since 1996, opening the Friday before Thanksgiving and running through Christmas Eve. Wooden huts sell hand-carved ornaments, nutcrackers, beeswax candles and roasted nuts; the real ritual is a mug of hot gluhwein in the year's collectible boot mug, which you can keep or return for your deposit back. Admission is free. Come on a weekday evening if you can - weekend afternoons are shoulder to shoulder. Sister markets operate in Wrigleyville and Aurora, but the Daley Plaza original, under the Picasso sculpture and the city tree, is the one.
highlights: Free admission, late November to Christmas Eve
Collectible gluhwein boot mug each year
Daley Plaza setting under the Picasso
why_residents_love_it: Genuinely walkable from home - the closest thing River North has to a neighborhood holiday tradition.

name: Wintrust Magnificent Mile Lights Festival
address: N Michigan Ave from Oak St south to Wacker Dr, Chicago, IL 60611
distance_note: The parade route is about 0.6-0.8 miles east - a 12-15 minute walk straight down Ontario or Ohio to Michigan Avenue. This is the closest major parade to the building.
price_range: Free (grandstand and hotel viewing packages available)
description: The unofficial start of the Chicago holiday season, held on the Saturday before Thanksgiving - November 21 in 2026. Beginning at Oak Street, the parade moves south down Michigan Avenue and, block by block, illuminates more than a million lights in the trees along the Magnificent Mile, ending with fireworks over the river and Santa's arrival. Daytime programming on Lights Festival Lane runs free family activities before the parade. It is free to watch from the sidewalk; grab a spot on the east side of Michigan by mid-afternoon, or book a restaurant with a window if you'd rather stay warm.
highlights: One million-plus lights switched on block by block
Fireworks finale over the Chicago River
why_residents_love_it: Walk 12 minutes and you're at the front of the parade that kicks off Chicago's entire holiday season.

name: Lollapalooza
address: Grant Park, 331 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60601
distance_note: Grant Park is about 1.3 miles southeast - a 25-minute walk down Michigan Avenue, or a short Red Line ride to Monroe. Expect major street closures on Columbus and Balbo during the festival.
price_range: $$$$ (four-day passes several hundred dollars; single days less)
description: Four days, eight stages and roughly 400,000 people take over Grant Park at the end of every July - the 2026 edition ran July 30 through August 2. Lollapalooza has been Chicago's summer anchor since it planted itself here in 2005, drawing headliners across rock, pop, hip-hop and electronic music, plus a well-run Kidzapalooza area for families. Four-day passes sell out fast, often before the lineup is announced, and single-day tickets go on sale in spring. Even without a wristband the city fills with aftershows at clubs and theaters all week, several of them within walking distance of River North.
highlights: Four days, eight stages, late July/early August
why_residents_love_it: Walking distance to one of the biggest festivals in North America - and you get to sleep in your own bed.

name: Riot Fest
address: Douglass Park, 1401 S Sacramento Dr, Chicago, IL 60623
distance_note: Douglass Park is about 5 miles west-southwest. Take the Pink Line to California and walk about 10 minutes, roughly 35-40 minutes total from River North.
description: Chicago's scrappier, louder answer to Lollapalooza: three days in mid-September in Douglass Park - September 18-20 in 2026 - with over 100 bands across punk, rock, metal, alternative and hip-hop. The signature move is booking legacy acts to play a classic album front to back, which makes the lineup a nostalgia trip and a discovery engine at once. Carnival rides, a sideshow midway and genuinely good food vendors round it out. Single-day and three-day tickets both sell, and it is noticeably cheaper than the bigger festivals. Take the Pink Line rather than driving.
why_residents_love_it: The lineup skews toward bands you grew up on, and single-day tickets make it an easy one-off.

name: Chicago Pride Parade
address: Steps off at N Broadway & W Montrose Ave, ending near W Diversey Pkwy & N Sheridan Rd
distance_note: The route is roughly 4-5 miles north. Take the Red Line from Chicago/State to Sheridan or Addison - about 20 minutes; service is heavy but frequent on parade day.
description: One of the largest Pride parades in the country, drawing hundreds of thousands to the North Side on the last Sunday in June - June 28 in 2026, stepping off at 11 a.m. from Broadway and Montrose and running south to Diversey and Sheridan. The route cuts straight through Northalsted, the historic heart of Chicago's LGBTQ+ community, and the whole weekend is stacked with events including Pride Fest on Halsted the week before. Arrive early for a curb spot, take the Red Line rather than driving, and expect the entire neighborhood to be closed to traffic well before the first float.
highlights: Last Sunday in June, 11 a.m. step-off
Pride Fest on Halsted the preceding weekend
why_residents_love_it: A short train ride to one of the biggest, warmest street celebrations in the country.

name: Chicago St. Patrick's Day Parade & River Dyeing
address: River dyeing along the Chicago River between Columbus Dr and State St; parade on Columbus Dr from Balbo Dr to Monroe St
distance_note: The river dyeing happens roughly 0.8 miles southeast - a 15-minute walk down Orleans and across to the Riverwalk. You can be at a bridge rail before the first boat passes.
description: Chicago's most photographed tradition happens on the Saturday before St. Patrick's Day. The Plumbers Local 130 crew dyes the Chicago River a startling emerald green starting at 10 a.m. - in 2026 that fell on Saturday, March 14 - and the color holds for several hours. The downtown parade steps off just after noon on Columbus Drive between Balbo and Monroe. Best river views are from the Riverwalk and the Michigan, Columbus and Wabash bridges; get there by 9:15 for a rail spot. A separate South Side Irish Parade runs in Beverly the following weekend. Dress warm - mid-March here is not spring.
highlights: River dyeing at 10 a.m., Saturday before St. Patrick's Day
Downtown parade on Columbus Drive just after noon
Bridge and Riverwalk viewpoints fill by 9:15 a.m.
why_residents_love_it: One of the few genuinely unique-to-Chicago spectacles, and it happens 15 minutes from the front door.

name: Navy Pier Summer Fireworks
address: Navy Pier, 600 E Grand Ave, Chicago, IL 60611
distance_note: Navy Pier is about 1.5 miles east - a 30-minute walk or 8-minute ride. Ohio Street Beach at 1.3 miles is the closest quality viewing spot, and many River North rooftops see it directly.
description: Navy Pier launches free fireworks over Lake Michigan twice a week all summer - Wednesdays around 9 p.m. and Saturdays around 10 p.m., from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day. The shows are choreographed to music and last roughly ten minutes. You do not need to be on the Pier: the view from Ohio Street Beach, Olive Park and the Lakefront Trail is arguably better and far less crowded, and plenty of River North rooftops catch it clean. The Pier also runs a New Year's Eve show. Everything is free; only the rides, boat cruises and restaurants cost money.
highlights: Free, Wednesdays and Saturdays all summer
Great views from Ohio Street Beach and Olive Park
why_residents_love_it: Twice-weekly fireworks you can often watch from the roof deck without leaving the building.

name: O'Hare & Midway Airport Access
address: O'Hare International: 10000 W O'Hare Ave, Chicago, IL 60666 | Midway International: 5700 S Cicero Ave, Chicago, IL 60638
distance_note: O'Hare: ~17 mi, 30-55 min by car; ~50-55 min total via Blue Line from Clark/Lake (a 12-minute walk or one Brown Line stop away). Midway: ~12 mi, 25-40 min by car; ~40 min via Orange Line from Washington/Wells.
description: Two major airports, both reachable without a car. For O'Hare, roughly 17 miles northwest, the Blue Line from Clark/Lake runs 24 hours and takes about 45 minutes for $5 outbound - reliable even when the Kennedy Expressway is not. Driving is 30 minutes at 6 a.m. and can stretch past an hour at rush. For Midway, about 12 miles southwest, take the Orange Line from Washington/Wells - roughly 30 minutes and $2.50 - or drive it in 25 to 40 minutes. Both trains beat rideshare on cost and, during peak traffic, on time.
highlights: Blue Line to O'Hare runs 24 hours, ~45 min
Orange Line to Midway, ~30 min for $2.50
Trains beat driving during rush hour
why_residents_love_it: A 24-hour train to O'Hare removes the single most stressful part of every early flight.

name: Divvy Bike Share
address: Docking stations throughout River North; system-wide across Chicago and Evanston
distance_note: Multiple docking stations sit within a 2-5 minute walk of 401 W Ontario throughout River North. Check the Divvy or Lyft app for live dock and bike availability before heading out.
price_range: $ (single ride ~$1 + per minute; day pass ~$20; annual membership available)
description: Chicago's city-owned bike share, operated by Lyft, with docking stations scattered every few blocks through River North and thousands of classic and electric bikes across the system. Single rides start around $1 plus a per-minute charge; a day pass runs about $20 for unlimited three-hour rides, and an annual membership makes short trips essentially free. Use the Divvy or Lyft app to find the nearest dock with available bikes before you walk out - availability shifts fast during commute hours. The Lakefront Trail is a ten-minute ride east and is the best reason to use it.
highlights: Docks every few blocks in River North
Lakefront Trail about 10 minutes away by bike
why_residents_love_it: Faster than a rideshare for anything under two miles, and the ride to the lakefront takes ten minutes.

name: Metra: Ogilvie Transportation Center & Union Station
address: Ogilvie: 500 W Madison St, Chicago, IL 60661 | Union Station: 225 S Canal St, Chicago, IL 60606
distance_note: Ogilvie is about 1.1 miles southwest - a 20-22 minute walk, or 8 minutes by car. Union Station is about 1.4 miles, roughly 27 minutes on foot. The Brown Line to Washington/Wells puts you within three blocks of either.
price_range: $$ (Metra fares vary by zone; Amtrak varies)
description: The two downtown terminals that connect River North to the suburbs and, at Union Station, to Amtrak's national network. Ogilvie handles the Union Pacific North, Northwest and West lines - the North line is the one to know, running to Evanston, Wilmette and the North Shore. Union Station covers the BNSF and Milwaukee District lines plus every Amtrak departure from Chicago. Both are open early and late, and both have solid food halls if you're waiting. Buy Metra tickets in the Ventra app rather than on board, where fares cost more.
highlights: Union Station: BNSF, Milwaukee District and all Amtrak
Buy tickets in the Ventra app to avoid onboard surcharges
why_residents_love_it: Both suburban rail terminals and every Amtrak train are inside a 20-minute walk or a short ride.

name: River North Pet Care: PUPS Pet Club & Companion Animal Hospital
address: PUPS Pet Club: 316 W Illinois St, Chicago, IL 60654 | Companion Animal Hospital: 749 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60654
distance_note: PUPS Pet Club is 0.15 miles south - a 3-minute walk down Orleans to Illinois Street. Companion Animal Hospital is about 0.5 miles east on Clark, a 10-minute walk.
description: Two blocks south of the building, PUPS Pet Club's River North location handles dog daycare, overnight boarding, grooming and training, and is open 365 days a year for boarding - which matters around holidays when everything else is full. Daycare gets your dog out of the apartment on a long workday and is bookable by the day or in discounted packages. For medical care, Companion Animal Hospital River North on Clark Street is the nearest full-service vet, offering wellness exams, vaccines, dentistry and same-day sick visits, plus grooming. Both book up; register your pet before you actually need them.
highlights: Open 365 days a year for boarding
Companion Animal Hospital is the closest full-service vet
why_residents_love_it: Daycare is a three-minute walk, so a long workday or a last-minute trip stops being a crisis.

name: Dry Cleaning & Laundry in River North
address: Neighborhood options include Orleans Cleaners in River North and Imperial Cleaners, 1221 N Dearborn St, Chicago, IL 60610
distance_note: Multiple walk-in cleaners sit within a 3-8 minute walk along Orleans, Wells and Clark. Delivery services pick up directly at the building, typically next-day return.
description: Two practical routes. Walk-in: several small cleaners operate along Orleans, Wells and Clark within a few blocks, with typical two-to-three-day turnaround and same-day service if you drop off before 9 a.m. Pickup and delivery: services like Press Cleaners and Laundryheap cover River North with app-scheduled door pickup, free delivery on most orders and same-day or next-day return - genuinely worth it if your building has a package room or front desk that can hold garments. Compare per-piece pricing before committing; downtown rates vary widely for the same shirt.
highlights: Walk-in cleaners within a few blocks on Orleans and Wells
App-based pickup and delivery covers River North
Same-day service with early morning drop-off
why_residents_love_it: Between the walk-in shops on Wells and the app-based pickup services, dry cleaning never requires a detour.

name: Jewel-Osco (River North)
distance_note: About 0.7 miles east - a 13-15 minute walk down Ontario and over to State Street. Delivery or a short rideshare is the move for a big shop.
description: The full-size, everything-under-one-roof grocery option nearby: real produce and meat departments, a deli, a floral counter, and an in-store pharmacy that handles transfers and most insurance. It's the store to use for a genuine weekly shop rather than a fill-in run. Delivery and curbside pickup are available through the Jewel-Osco app, which is worth setting up if you'd rather not carry bags eight blocks. Prices run lower than the specialty grocers, and the digital coupons in the app are the difference between a fine bill and a good one.
highlights: Delivery and curbside pickup via app
Best pricing of the nearby full-size stores
why_residents_love_it: The one nearby store that covers a full week's groceries and prescriptions in a single stop.

name: Target - Chicago River North
distance_note: About 0.3 miles east - a 5-6 minute walk down Ontario to LaSalle. The nearest one-stop store to the building.
description: The closest big-box store to the building and the workhorse for everything that isn't food: cleaning supplies, paper goods, over-the-counter medicine, small appliances, phone chargers, seasonal decor. highlights: Order Pickup and Drive Up available
why_residents_love_it: Five minutes on foot for anything you forgot, from paper towels to a phone charger.

name: Whole Foods Market - One Chicago
address: 3 W Chicago Ave, Floors 1-2, Chicago, IL 60654

highlights: Two floors, open 8 a.m.-10 p.m. daily
Large hot bar and prepared foods

name: Walgreens (641 N Clark St) - 24 Hours

name: Chicago Public Library - Near North Branch
distance_note: About 0.7 miles north - a 13-14 minute walk straight up Orleans Street to Division. Also a short ride on the #37 Sedgwick bus.
description: The neighborhood branch, a striking Josef Paul Kleihues-designed building at Division and Franklin. Quiet study space and free Wi-Fi

description: Four rail stations serve this block of River North. highlights: Grand and Chicago Red Line stops 13-16 minutes east
why_residents_love_it: Two rail lines within a ten-minute walk means most residents genuinely don't need a car.

name: Trader Joe's (River North)

description: Straight down Ontario Street from the building - the same street, just east of Michigan Avenue - which makes this the easiest walkable grocery run in the neighborhood. why_residents_love_it: Same street, ten minutes, and you can carry the whole trip home in two bags.
